rationale: The literature partially supports the finding that cutaneous interferonopathy-like signs occur in a small minority of STISS patients: Isidor et al. (2022) identified chilblains in exactly 2 of 24 individuals (~8.3%). However, another cohort of 6 patients from two unrelated families documented that 0 of 6 had clinical autoinflammatory signs and noted that observed IFN-I gene signature perturbations were non-specific. Furthermore, the claim that chilblains reliably discriminate STISS from phenotypically overlapping non-proteasomal syndromes like Cornelia de Lange or Rubinstein-Taybi is not substantiated by any comparative data in the retrieved literature.

evidence.text: In a cohort of 24 unrelated individuals with PSMD12 pathogenic variants, 2 individuals (8.3%) displayed chilblains resembling features of autoinflammatory interferonopathies, alongside upregulation of type I interferon-stimulated genes.

source.title: Stankiewicz-Isidor syndrome: expanding the clinical and molecular phenotype
source.quote: Of note, 2 patients also showed chilblains resembling signs observed in interferonopathy. Remarkably, our data show that STISS patient cells exhibit a profound remodeling of the mTORC1 and mitophagy pathways with an induction of type I interferon-stimulated genes.

evidence.text: In an independent familial cohort of 6 individuals with PSMD12 variants, none presented with clinical manifestations of autoinflammation, and observed type I interferon signature perturbations were found to be non-specific.

source.title: Stankiewicz-Isidor syndrome
source.quote: None presented clinical manifestations of autoinflammation and the detected IFN-I signature perturbations were not specific.

evidence.text: Heterozygous loss-of-function variants in 19S proteasome cap genes, including PSMD12, define neurodevelopmental proteasomopathies linked to type I interferon signaling, distinct from classical monogenic lupus or pure autoinflammatory interferonopathies.

source.title: Emerging concepts and treatments in autoinflammatory interferonopathies and monogenic systemic lupus erythematosus
source.quote: of neurodevelopmental proteasomopathies caused by heterozygous LOF mutations in genes encoding components or assembly units of the 19S regulatory cap including PSMD12

conflicts: While Isidor et al. (2022) found chilblains in 2 of 24 individuals (8.3%) and proposed interferon gene signature activation as a diagnostic hallmark, an independent cohort of 6 patients from two families identified no clinical autoinflammation and concluded that IFN-I signature perturbations were non-specific.

The literature does not evaluate or substantiate the discriminative power of chilblains between STISS and phenotypically overlapping syndromes such as Cornelia de Lange syndrome or Rubinstein-Taybi syndrome.

new_directions.question_text: What is the true prevalence and specificity of cutaneous chilblains and IFN-I biomarker signatures across an unselected, international multi-cohort registry of PSMD12-affected individuals?
new_directions.rationale: Current cohorts show conflicting rates and disputed specificity of the interferonopathy phenotype, ranging from 8.3% to 0%.

new_directions.question_text: How frequently do pernio/chilblain-like lesions occur in non-proteasomal neurodevelopmental disorders like Cornelia de Lange or Rubinstein-Taybi syndromes compared to STISS?
new_directions.rationale: Direct comparative cohort data are required to validate whether cutaneous chilblains have positive discriminative utility against clinical phenocopies.
